title: Heinrich Lukacs - Communication From, Requesting Permission To Organize Lotteries Of Valuables

page_data.en:

Special Branch
March 18, 1942
H. LUKACS - Communication from, requesting
permission to organize lotteries of
valuables.
Heinrich LUKACS, German Jewish refugee, born
at Eisenstadt on September 5, 1888, who arrived in
Shanghai from Europe in November 1938, has been
interviewed in respect of the contents of his letter
dated February 20, 1942 addressed to the Shanghai
Municipal Council in which he applies for permission
to organize lotteries of valuables.
The applicant, who is financially supported
in his existence by the Committee for the Assistance
of European Jewish refugees in Shanghai and who was
formerly a refugee camp inmate is, himself, without
funds, and extremely vague as to what he intends to
do in the organizing of the proposed lottery. He
states that if he secures permission from the Municipal
Council to operate any kind of lottery it is his
intention to approach Japanese or Chinese sources
for sufficient funds to provide the initial outlay
for the venture. He has not the slightest idea
at present as to where the gaming tables would be
located and when questioned as to where he would
find patrons to gamble for 30,000 objects daily
(a statement he makes in his communication), he made
no reply.
LUKACS talks about offering prizes such as an
Omega gold watch, an order for a suit of clothes, a
pair of shoes, a silver samovar, etc., etc. and he
also mentions that of every 2½ to three tickets
sold one would secure a prize. Taking into consideration

H. LUKACS - 来函，请求

海因里希·卢卡克斯（Heinrich LUKACS），德籍犹太难民，1888年9月5日出生于艾森施塔特（Eisenstadt），于1938年11月从欧洲抵达上海，已就其1942年2月20日致上海工部局信函的内容接受问询，他在信中申请获准组织贵重物品彩票。
申请人目前的生活费用由上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会资助，他以前是难民营的收容人员，本人身无分文，且对于拟议中的彩票组织工作意图极为含糊。他表示，如果获得工部局批准经营任何形式的彩票，他打算向日本或中方渠道寻求足够资金，以提供该 ventures 的初始支出。他目前对于赌桌将设在何处毫无头绪，当被问及从哪里寻找每天为30,000件物品下注的赌客时（这是他在来信中的说法），他未作回答。
卢卡克斯谈到提供诸如欧米茄金表、一套服装的订单、一双鞋、一个银质茶炊等奖品，等等，他还提到，每售出两枚半至三枚彩票，就有一枚能中奖。考虑到

ation the cost of such prizes as quoted higher
(they would not, of course, all be of such value)
the price of tickets would necessarily have to be
high, though LUKACS, vague as ever, cannot give any
indication as to the likely prices of tickets.
While it is appreciated that Central European
refugees would benefit by the scheme, were it allowed,
and they definitely do require financial support
in these stringent times, LUKACS and his unknown
financial backers would also line their pockets to
a considerable extent. While LUKACS may be credited
with a praiseworthy attempt to assist Jewish refugees
in these critical times, it ought to be pointed out
that a properly constituted Committee is in existence
for the caring of such refugees and this Committee
has not, up to the present, evinced the slightest
desire to conduct anything slightly resembling the
matter under question.
LUKACS could not even state, when asked, whether
the gambling was more or less expressly designed to
take place in refugee or non-refugee circles, but
in any event, when consideration is given to stagnation
in trade and the nebulosity of the intended scheme
it is extremely doubtful whether such a plan would
be feasible.
As a matter of interest it should also be pointed
out that in the event of permission being granted
for this lottery to be operated, similar requests are
almost certain to be received.

上述奖品的成本较高（当然，并非所有奖品都具有如此高的价值），彩票价格必然不得不定得很高，尽管卢卡克斯一如既往地含糊其辞，无法对彩票的可能价格给出任何指示。
虽然人们认识到，如果该计划被允许，中欧难民将从中受益，而且在这些严峻时期他们确实需要财政支持，但卢卡克斯及其不知名的财务支持者也将借此大捞一笔。虽然卢卡克斯在这些危急时刻试图帮助犹太难民的举动值得称赞，但必须指出的是，目前已有一个正式组成的委员会负责照顾此类难民，而该委员会迄今为止并未表现出丝毫意愿去开展任何与所涉事项稍许类似的活动。
当被问及时，卢卡克斯甚至无法说明赌博活动是更明确地针对难民圈子还是非难民圈子进行，但无论如何，考虑到贸易停滞以及拟议计划的模糊性，这种计划是否可行极其值得怀疑。
出于关注，还应指出，如果批准经营此彩票，几乎肯定会收到类似的请求。
根据查阅的警务档案，在此期间，工部局从未批准过
